# String cleaning in Pandas

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

print("=== Creating data with messy strings ===\n")

data = {
    'Name': ['  Aragorn  ', 'LEGOLAS', 'Gimli!', 'gandalf', 'Frodo',
             '  Sam  ', 'Merry', 'Pippin  ', 'Boromir', 'Gollum '],
    'Class': ['WARRIOR', 'Archer', 'dwarf', 'WIZARD', 'hobbit',
              'Hobbit', 'HOBbit', 'HOBBIT', 'warrior', 'Creature'],
    'Join_Date': ['2024-01-15', '2024-02-20', '2024-03-10',
                  '2024-04-05', '2024-01-01', '2024-01-02',
                  '2024-01-03', '2024-01-04', '2024-02-01', '2024-01-10']
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
print(f"Original DataFrame:")
print(df)

print("\n=== Cleaning whitespace ===\n")

# Remove leading/trailing whitespace
df['Name'] = df['Name'].str.strip()
print(f"After strip():\n{df['Name']}")

print("\n=== Changing case ===\n")

# Lowercase
df['Name_lower'] = df['Name'].str.lower()
print(f"Lowercase:\n{df['Name_lower']}")

# Uppercase
df['Name_upper'] = df['Name'].str.upper()
print(f"Uppercase:\n{df['Name_upper']}")

# Title case
df['Name_title'] = df['Name'].str.title()
print(f"Title case:\n{df['Name_title']}")

print("\n=== Removing special characters ===\n")

# Remove specific characters
df['Name_clean'] = df['Name'].str.replace('!', '', regex=False)
print(f"After removing '!':\n{df['Name_clean']}")

# Remove all non-alphanumeric
# df['Name_clean'] = df['Name'].str.replace(r'[^a-zA-Z0-9\s]', '', regex=True)

print("\n=== Standardizing categorical data ===\n")

# Standardize Class column
print(f"Before standardization:\n{df['Class'].value_counts()}")

df['Class'] = df['Class'].str.lower().str.title()
df['Class'] = df['Class'].replace({
    'Hobbit': 'Hobbit',
    'Warrior': 'Warrior',
    'Wizard': 'Wizard',
    'Archer': 'Archer',
    'Dwarf': 'Dwarf',
    'Creature': 'Creature'
})

print(f"\nAfter standardization:\n{df['Class'].value_counts()}")

print("\n=== Extracting parts of strings ===\n")

# Extract first 3 characters
df['Name_abbr'] = df['Name'].str[:3]
print(f"Name abbreviation:\n{df['Name_abbr']}")

# Extract after space
# df['Name'] = df['Name'].str.extract(r'^(\w+)')

print("\n=== Checking string properties ===\n")

# Check if names are in title case
print(f"Is title case?\n{df['Name'].str.istitle()}")

# Check if names contain 'a'
print(f"\nContains 'a'?\n{df['Name'].str.contains('a', case=False)}")

print("\n=== String length ===\n")

df['Name_length'] = df['Name'].str.len()
print(f"Name lengths:\n{df[['Name', 'Name_length']]}")

phase1.explanation:
🐍 **String cleaning fixes text inconsistencies.**

**String methods in Pandas:**
```python
df['col'].str.strip()      # Remove whitespace
df['col'].str.lower()      # Lowercase
df['col'].str.upper()      # Uppercase
df['col'].str.title()      # Title case
df['col'].str.replace()    # Replace text
df['col'].str.contains()   # Check pattern
df['col'].str.len()        # String length
df['col'].str[:3]          # Slicing
```

**Cleaning patterns:**
```python
# Standardize categories
df['col'] = df['col'].str.lower().str.title()

# Remove special characters
df['col'] = df['col'].str.replace('[^a-zA-Z0-9\s]', '', regex=True)

# Remove whitespace
df['col'] = df['col'].str.strip()

# Extract parts
df['col'] = df['col'].str.extract(r'^(\w+)')
```

**Python-chan says:**
"String cleaning is essential for text data. Clean strings = clean analysis."

phase2.explanation:
**String operations fail on NaN values!**

**What's wrong:**
1. `str.lower()` doesn't work on NaN
2. Returns NaN or raises error

**The fix:**
```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

df = pd.DataFrame({'Name': ['Aragorn', np.nan, 'Legolas', None]})

# Method 1: Fill NaN first
df['clean1'] = df['Name'].fillna('').str.lower()

# Method 2: Use na parameter
df['clean2'] = df['Name'].str.lower(na='')

# Method 3: Use na parameter with None
df['clean3'] = df['Name'].str.lower(na=None)

# Method 4: Use a function with error handling
def clean_name(name):
    if pd.isna(name):
        return ''
    return name.lower()

df['clean4'] = df['Name'].apply(clean_name)

print(df)
```

**Python-chan says:**
"Always handle NaN before string operations. Use `na` parameter or fillna."
